scenes.heading: Genes and chromosomes
scenes.sub: How do two metres of DNA fit inside one nucleus?
scenes.say: Your DNA holds roughly twenty thousand genes. They're packed into chromosomes, so each cell can store about two metres of DNA inside a nucleus far too small to see.
scenes.caption: Your DNA holds roughly 20,000 genes. They're packed into chromosomes, so each cell can store about 2 metres of DNA inside a nucleus far too small to see.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A cookbook, a recipe, its page, and versions of that recipe
scenes.science: A chromosome, a gene, its locus, and its alleles
scenes.breaks: cells read genes automatically, and a gene usually codes for one protein, not a whole meal.
scenes.say: Think of a chromosome as a cookbook. A gene is one recipe, and its locus is the page number. Different versions of that recipe, like a cake with or without nuts, are alleles.

scenes.heading: Chromosomes
points: Two sister chromatids joined at a centromere
scenes.say: A chromosome is one long DNA molecule wrapped around histone proteins, like a hose wound on a reel. Before a cell divides, the DNA has been copied, so each chromosome is two identical sister chromatids joined at the centromere. One X shape is still one chromosome.

scenes.heading: Homologous pairs vs sister chromatids

left.title: Homologous pair
points: One from Mum, one from Dad

scenes.say: Don't mix these up. Homologous chromosomes come one from Mum and one from Dad. They carry the same genes, but maybe different alleles. Sister chromatids are identical copies made when DNA is copied.

scenes.heading: 46 = 23 pairs
points: Pair 23: sex chromosomes, XX or XY
scenes.say: Human body cells have forty-six chromosomes in twenty-three pairs. Twenty-two pairs are autosomes, and the last pair is the sex chromosomes, XX or XY. Body cells are diploid. Sperm and eggs are haploid, with twenty-three. A karyotype shows chromosome number and shape, but not alleles.
scenes.caption: Human body cells have 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs. 22 pairs are autosomes, and the last pair is the sex chromosomes, XX or XY. Body cells are diploid. Sperm and eggs are haploid, with 23. A karyotype shows chromosome number and shape, but not alleles.

scenes.heading: DNA → mRNA → protein
steps: mRNA uses U instead of T
Read in triplets: 1 per amino acid
scenes.say: To make a protein, the gene is first copied into mRNA in the nucleus. That's transcription, and RNA uses U instead of T. Then a ribosome reads the mRNA three bases at a time and joins the matching amino acids. That's translation.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: A gene section is 18 bases long. How many amino acids does it code for? What mRNA pairs with DNA triplet TAC?
lines: One amino acid per triplet of 3 bases
T → A, A → U, C → G
scenes.say: A gene section is eighteen bases long. Eighteen divided by three gives six amino acids. And for the DNA triplet T A C, the mRNA uses U for T's partner, so it becomes A U G.
scenes.caption: A gene section is 18 bases long. 18 ÷ 3 gives 6 amino acids. And for the DNA triplet TAC, the mRNA uses U, so it becomes AUG.

points: Alleles are versions of a gene
DNA → mRNA → protein, read in threes
scenes.say: Quick recap. Chromosomes are DNA wrapped around histones. Genes sit at fixed loci, and alleles are different versions. Body cells have forty-six chromosomes and gametes twenty-three. Now try the practice questions!
